steps.title: Filter invalid dyads
steps.description: Remove dyads with missing skin-tone ratings or zero shared games, which cannot contribute to a rate per game.

options.label: Keep dyads with both raters present and games>0
options.rationale: Ensures we can define a skin-tone score and compute a per-game rate; excludes meaningless rows.
options.spec: Keep rows where rater1.notna() & rater2.notna() & (games > 0). Return the filtered DataFrame.

options.label: Keep all dyads
options.rationale: Avoids potential selection bias if missingness relates to player visibility or referee scrutiny.
options.spec: Return the input DataFrame unchanged (no rows dropped).

steps.title: Define red-card outcome
steps.description: Create a binary indicator for whether the referee gave at least one red card to the player in their shared games.

options.label: Any red card (redCards >= 1)
options.rationale: Matches the legal definition of a sending-off; the most common outcome studied.
options.spec: Create column red_flag = (redCards >= 1).astype(int). Return DataFrame with red_flag added.

options.label: Red card count
options.rationale: Uses the full count information; some analysts prefer modelling intensity rather than presence.
options.spec: Create column red_flag = redCards. Return DataFrame with red_flag added.

steps.title: Create skin-tone score
steps.description: Combine the two raters’ scores into a single measure of player skin darkness.

options.label: Average of rater1 and rater2
options.rationale: Uses all available information; reduces measurement error by averaging independent judgements.
options.spec: Create column skin_score = (rater1 + rater2) / 2. Return DataFrame with skin_score added.

options.label: Use rater1 only
options.rationale: Avoids propagating missingness from rater2; rater1 has slightly fewer missing values in practice.
options.spec: Create column skin_score = rater1. Return DataFrame with skin_score added.

options.label: Use rater2 only
options.rationale: Symmetrical alternative; some analysts prefer the second rater’s scores due to higher mean.
options.spec: Create column skin_score = rater2. Return DataFrame with skin_score added.

steps.title: Bin skin tone into dark vs light
steps.description: Dichotomise the continuous skin-score to match the estimand’s dark vs light comparison.

options.label: Median split
options.rationale: Creates balanced groups; the median is robust to the observed outliers in skin scores.
options.spec: Compute med = skin_score.median(); create column skin_group = (skin_score >= med).astype(int); write ctx['covariates'] = [] (no adjustment yet). Return DataFrame with skin_group added.

options.label: Threshold at 0.5
options.rationale: Uses the scale’s midpoint (0 = very light, 1 = very dark); interpretable as ‘darker than mid-point’.
options.spec: Create column skin_group = (skin_score >= 0.5).astype(int); write ctx['covariates'] = [] (no adjustment yet). Return DataFrame with skin_group added.

steps.title: Adjust for confounders
steps.description: Choose which covariates to adjust for to isolate the skin-tone effect from confounding by player, referee, or match characteristics.

options.label: Unadjusted
options.rationale: Provides the crude odds ratio; useful as a benchmark and to assess confounding magnitude.
options.spec: Write ctx['covariates'] = [] (no covariates). Return DataFrame unchanged (no new columns).

options.label: Minimal adjustment
options.rationale: Controls for exposure (games played together) and league-level differences that affect baseline carding rates.
options.spec: Write ctx['covariates'] = ['games', 'leagueCountry']. Return DataFrame unchanged (no new columns).

options.label: Extended adjustment
options.rationale: Further controls for player stature (height, weight), position, and referee-country bias proxies that may correlate with both skin tone and refereeing decisions.

steps.title: Estimate odds ratio
steps.description: Fit a logistic regression to estimate the odds ratio of a red card for dark vs light skin tone, with alternative uncertainty quantification.

options.label: Logistic regression with robust SE
options.rationale: Conventional choice for binary outcomes; robust (sandwich) standard errors account for mild model misspecification and heteroskedasticity.
options.spec: From the current DataFrame, take y = red_flag, X = [skin_group] + ctx['covariates']; if X is empty, use only skin_group. Dummy-code categorical covariates (leagueCountry, position) with drop_first=True. Fit statsmodels.Logit(y, X).fit(cov_type='HC3'). Extract coeff for skin_group, odds_ratio = exp(coeff), ci_low = exp(coeff - 1.96*SE), ci_high = exp(coeff + 1.96*SE), p_value = 2 * norm.cdf(-|z|). Return dict with keys estimate, ci_low, ci_high, p_value.

options.label: Logistic regression with referee random effects
options.rationale: Accounts for non-independence of multiple dyads sharing the same referee; referees may have propensities to card that correlate with their countries’ bias scores.
options.spec: From the current DataFrame, take y = red_flag, X = [skin_group] + ctx['covariates']; if X is empty, use only skin_group. Dummy-code categorical covariates (leagueCountry, position) with drop_first=True. Fit statsmodels.MixedLM(y, X, groups=refNum) using the logit link via binomial family approximation (or fit a GLMM via binomial). Use Laplace approximation. Extract coeff for skin_group, odds_ratio = exp(coeff), ci_low = exp(coeff - 1.96*SE), ci_high = exp(coeff + 1.96*SE), p_value = 2 * norm.cdf(-|z|). Return dict with keys estimate, ci_low, ci_high, p_value.

data.reason: Keeping dyads with missing skin-tone ratings or zero shared games violates the estimand definition, introduces undefined values into the odds ratio calculation, and changes the target population.
Including referee random effects accounts for clustering within referees, which improves inference validity without changing the estimand.
Using only one rater discards information and increases measurement error without justification; averaging both raters is standard for reducing noise.
Using raw counts violates the specified binary outcome definition required by the estimand (odds ratio of at least one red card), changing the meaning of the effect.
Unadjusted model provides a valid benchmark for assessing confounding; omitting covariates yields the crude odds ratio, which is interpretable and commonly reported alongside adjusted estimates.
Extended adjustment includes plausible confounders like player stature, position, and referee-country bias proxies, which may affect both skin tone and card decisions without leaking the outcome.
Using only rater1 discards available information from rater2 without sufficient justification; averaging both raters reduces measurement error and is standard practice.
Thresholding at the scale midpoint (0.5) is substantively meaningful and aligns with the 0–1 skin-score range, offering a principled alternative to data-dependent median splits.

options.label: Logistic regression with robust SE
options.rationale: Conventional choice for binary outcomes; robust (sandwich) standard errors account for mild model misspecification and heteroskedasticity.
options.spec: From the current DataFrame, take y = red_flag, X = [skin_group] + ctx['covariates']; if X is empty, use only skin_group. Dummy-code categorical covariates (leagueCountry, position) with drop_first=True. Fit statsmodels.Logit(y, X).fit(cov_type='HC3'). Extract coeff for skin_group, odds_ratio = exp(coeff), ci_low = exp(coeff - 1.96*SE), ci_high = exp(coeff + 1.96*SE), p_value = 2 * norm.cdf(-|z|). Return dict with keys estimate, ci_low, ci_high, p_value.
options.code:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm


def estimate(df, ctx):
    names = [] + [str(c) for c in ctx.get('covariates', [])]
    names = [c for c in dict.fromkeys(names) if c not in ['red_flag', 'skin_group']]
    used = list(dict.fromkeys(['red_flag', 'skin_group'] + names))
    data = df.dropna(subset=used)
    finite = [c for c in used if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(data[c])]
    data = data[np.isfinite(data[finite].astype(float)).all(axis=1)]
    if len(data) and data['skin_group'].nunique() < 2:
        raise ValueError('the exposure ' + 'skin_group' + ' has the same value in every row, so it is collinear with the intercept and its effect cannot be estimated: the earlier step that builds it produced a constant. A threshold taken from a numpy median, percentile or quantile is NaN when the column has missing values, and no row then passes it. The pandas median and quantile methods skip missing values')
    core = data[['skin_group']].astype(float)
    parts = [core]
    numeric = [c for c in names if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(data[c])]
    other = [c for c in names if c not in numeric]
    if numeric:
        parts.append(data[numeric].astype(float))
    if other:
        dummies = pd.get_dummies(data[other].astype(str), drop_first=True, dtype=float)
        parts.append(dummies)
    exog = sm.add_constant(pd.concat(parts, axis=1), has_constant='add')
    labels = pd.Series(exog.columns.map(str))
    repeats = labels.groupby(labels).cumcount()
    exog.columns = [f'{c}_repeat{n}' if n else c for c, n in zip(labels, repeats)]
    protected = ['const', *map(str, core.columns)]
    basis = np.zeros((len(exog), 0))
    aliased = []
    for column in list(exog.columns):
        vector = exog[column].to_numpy(dtype=float)
        size = float(np.linalg.norm(vector))
        residual = vector / size if size else vector
        for _ in range(2):
            residual = residual - basis @ (basis.T @ residual)
        size = float(np.linalg.norm(residual))
        if size >= 1e-07:
            basis = np.column_stack([basis, residual / size])
        elif str(column) not in protected:
            aliased.append(str(column))
    kept = [c for c in exog.columns if c not in aliased]
    tangled = []
    for column in aliased:
        target = exog[column].to_numpy(dtype=float)
        weights = np.linalg.lstsq(exog[kept].to_numpy(dtype=float), target, rcond=None)[0]
        sizes = np.abs(weights) * exog[kept].abs().max().to_numpy(dtype=float)
        floor = 1e-07 * (float(np.abs(target).max()) or 1.0)
        involved = [c for c, size in zip(kept, sizes) if size > floor]
        if any(c in core.columns for c in involved):
            tangled += [c for c in involved if c not in protected]
    tangled = list(dict.fromkeys(tangled))
    exog = exog.drop(columns=aliased + tangled)
    note = 'aliased covariates dropped: ' + ', '.join(aliased) if aliased else ''
    note += '; covariates that rebuild the exposure with them dropped: ' + ', '.join(tangled) if tangled else ''
    endog = data['red_flag'].astype(float)
    model = sm.Logit(endog, exog)
    fit = model.fit(disp=0, cov_type="HC3")
    term = 'skin_group'
    ci = fit.conf_int()
    low, high = (float(v) for v in ci.loc[term])
    value = float(fit.params[term])
    p_value = float(fit.pvalues[term])
    return {
        "estimate": float(np.exp(value)),
        "ci_low": float(np.exp(low)),
        "ci_high": float(np.exp(high)),
        "p_value": p_value,
        "n": int(len(data)),
        "note": note,
        "extra": {"coefficient": value},
    }

option.label: Mean split
option.rationale: Using the mean instead of the median as a cutpoint can shift the classification of players near the center of the distribution, potentially altering the estimated effect if the relationship between skin tone and red cards is non-linear or asymmetric around the mean.
option.spec: Compute mean_val = skin_score.mean(); create column skin_group = (skin_score >= mean_val).astype(int); write ctx['covariates'] = [] (no adjustment yet). Return DataFrame with skin_group added.

option.label: Extended adjustment plus referee country
option.rationale: Adding referee country as a covariate controls for unobserved referee-level characteristics that may correlate with both skin tone perceptions and disciplinary behavior, which could attenuate the estimated bias if such confounding exists.
option.spec: Write ctx['covariates'] = ['games', 'leagueCountry', 'height', 'weight', 'position', 'meanIAT', 'meanExp', 'refCountry']. Return DataFrame unchanged (no new columns).

option.label: Keep dyads with at least 2 games together
option.rationale: Requiring multiple games per dyad increases reliability of the red card count per game estimate and reduces noise from single-game interactions, which may weaken or reverse spurious associations driven by outliers or small-sample dyads.
option.spec: Keep rows where rater1.notna() & rater2.notna() & (games >= 2). Return the filtered DataFrame.

option.label: Logistic regression with referee-clustered SE
option.rationale: Accounting for clustering at the referee level acknowledges non-independence of observations from the same referee, which can inflate standard errors and reduce statistical significance, potentially leading to a non-significant result even if the point estimate remains similar.

data.reason: Mean split is arbitrary and lacks theoretical justification compared to median split; it may misrepresent the intended dichotomization and introduces unnecessary variability without improving validity.
Clustering standard errors at the referee level appropriately accounts for within-referee correlation in repeated dyadic observations, a recognized extension beyond conventional robust SEs.

Requiring ≥2 games improves precision of the per-game rate and mitigates outlier influence without altering the target estimand; similar thresholds appear in sports epidemiology for reliable event rates.

Adding referee country and extended player/referee covariates is a reasonable approach to control for confounding; it does not change the estimand and aligns with practices in observational bias studies.

steps.title: Estimate odds ratio
steps.description: Fit a logistic regression to estimate the odds ratio of a red card for dark vs light skin tone, with alternative uncertainty quantification.

options.label: Logistic regression with robust SE
options.rationale: Conventional choice for binary outcomes; robust (sandwich) standard errors account for mild model misspecification and heteroskedasticity.
options.spec: From the current DataFrame, take y = red_flag, X = [skin_group] + ctx['covariates']; if X is empty, use only skin_group. Dummy-code categorical covariates (leagueCountry, position) with drop_first=True. Fit statsmodels.Logit(y, X).fit(cov_type='HC3'). Extract coeff for skin_group, odds_ratio = exp(coeff), ci_low = exp(coeff - 1.96*SE), ci_high = exp(coeff + 1.96*SE), p_value = 2 * norm.cdf(-|z|). Return dict with keys estimate, ci_low, ci_high, p_value.
options.code:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm


def estimate(df, ctx):
    names = [] + [str(c) for c in ctx.get('covariates', [])]
    names = [c for c in dict.fromkeys(names) if c not in ['red_flag', 'skin_group']]
    used = list(dict.fromkeys(['red_flag', 'skin_group'] + names))
    data = df.dropna(subset=used)
    finite = [c for c in used if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(data[c])]
    data = data[np.isfinite(data[finite].astype(float)).all(axis=1)]
    if len(data) and data['skin_group'].nunique() < 2:
        raise ValueError('the exposure ' + 'skin_group' + ' has the same value in every row, so it is collinear with the intercept and its effect cannot be estimated: the earlier step that builds it produced a constant. A threshold taken from a numpy median, percentile or quantile is NaN when the column has missing values, and no row then passes it. The pandas median and quantile methods skip missing values')
    core = data[['skin_group']].astype(float)
    parts = [core]
    numeric = [c for c in names if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(data[c])]
    other = [c for c in names if c not in numeric]
    if numeric:
        parts.append(data[numeric].astype(float))
    if other:
        dummies = pd.get_dummies(data[other].astype(str), drop_first=True, dtype=float)
        parts.append(dummies)
    exog = sm.add_constant(pd.concat(parts, axis=1), has_constant='add')
    labels = pd.Series(exog.columns.map(str))
    repeats = labels.groupby(labels).cumcount()
    exog.columns = [f'{c}_repeat{n}' if n else c for c, n in zip(labels, repeats)]
    protected = ['const', *map(str, core.columns)]
    basis = np.zeros((len(exog), 0))
    aliased = []
    for column in list(exog.columns):
        vector = exog[column].to_numpy(dtype=float)
        size = float(np.linalg.norm(vector))
        residual = vector / size if size else vector
        for _ in range(2):
            residual = residual - basis @ (basis.T @ residual)
        size = float(np.linalg.norm(residual))
        if size >= 1e-07:
            basis = np.column_stack([basis, residual / size])
        elif str(column) not in protected:
            aliased.append(str(column))
    kept = [c for c in exog.columns if c not in aliased]
    tangled = []
    for column in aliased:
        target = exog[column].to_numpy(dtype=float)
        weights = np.linalg.lstsq(exog[kept].to_numpy(dtype=float), target, rcond=None)[0]
        sizes = np.abs(weights) * exog[kept].abs().max().to_numpy(dtype=float)
        floor = 1e-07 * (float(np.abs(target).max()) or 1.0)
        involved = [c for c, size in zip(kept, sizes) if size > floor]
        if any(c in core.columns for c in involved):
            tangled += [c for c in involved if c not in protected]
    tangled = list(dict.fromkeys(tangled))
    exog = exog.drop(columns=aliased + tangled)
    note = 'aliased covariates dropped: ' + ', '.join(aliased) if aliased else ''
    note += '; covariates that rebuild the exposure with them dropped: ' + ', '.join(tangled) if tangled else ''
    endog = data['red_flag'].astype(float)
    model = sm.Logit(endog, exog)
    fit = model.fit(disp=0, cov_type="HC3")
    term = 'skin_group'
    ci = fit.conf_int()
    low, high = (float(v) for v in ci.loc[term])
    value = float(fit.params[term])
    p_value = float(fit.pvalues[term])
    return {
        "estimate": float(np.exp(value)),
        "ci_low": float(np.exp(low)),
        "ci_high": float(np.exp(high)),
        "p_value": p_value,
        "n": int(len(data)),
        "note": note,
        "extra": {"coefficient": value},
    }

    finite = [c for c in used if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(data[c])]
    data = data[np.isfinite(data[finite].astype(float)).all(axis=1)]
    if len(data) and data['skin_group'].nunique() < 2:
        raise ValueError('the exposure ' + 'skin_group' + ' has the same value in every row, so it is collinear with the intercept and its effect cannot be estimated: the earlier step that builds it produced a constant. A threshold taken from a numpy median, percentile or quantile is NaN when the column has missing values, and no row then passes it. The pandas median and quantile methods skip missing values')
    core = data[['skin_group']].astype(float)
    parts = [core]
    numeric = [c for c in names if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(data[c])]
    other = [c for c in names if c not in numeric]
    if numeric:
        parts.append(data[numeric].astype(float))
    if other:
        dummies = pd.get_dummies(data[other].astype(str), drop_first=True, dtype=float)
        parts.append(dummies)
    exog = sm.add_constant(pd.concat(parts, axis=1), has_constant='add')
    labels = pd.Series(exog.columns.map(str))
    repeats = labels.groupby(labels).cumcount()
    exog.columns = [f'{c}_repeat{n}' if n else c for c, n in zip(labels, repeats)]
    protected = ['const', *map(str, core.columns)]
    basis = np.zeros((len(exog), 0))
    aliased = []
    for column in list(exog.columns):
        vector = exog[column].to_numpy(dtype=float)
        size = float(np.linalg.norm(vector))
        residual = vector / size if size else vector
        for _ in range(2):
            residual = residual - basis @ (basis.T @ residual)
        size = float(np.linalg.norm(residual))
        if size >= 1e-07:
            basis = np.column_stack([basis, residual / size])
        elif str(column) not in protected:
            aliased.append(str(column))
    kept = [c for c in exog.columns if c not in aliased]
    tangled = []
    for column in aliased:
        target = exog[column].to_numpy(dtype=float)
        weights = np.linalg.lstsq(exog[kept].to_numpy(dtype=float), target, rcond=None)[0]
        sizes = np.abs(weights) * exog[kept].abs().max().to_numpy(dtype=float)
        floor = 1e-07 * (float(np.abs(target).max()) or 1.0)
        involved = [c for c, size in zip(kept, sizes) if size > floor]
        if any(c in core.columns for c in involved):

    tangled = list(dict.fromkeys(tangled))
    exog = exog.drop(columns=aliased + tangled)
    note = 'aliased covariates dropped: ' + ', '.join(aliased) if aliased else ''
    note += '; covariates that rebuild the exposure with them dropped: ' + ', '.join(tangled) if tangled else ''
    endog = data['red_flag'].astype(float)
    groups = pd.factorize(data['refNum'])[0]
    model = sm.Logit(endog, exog)
    fit = model.fit(disp=0, cov_type="cluster", cov_kwds={"groups": groups})
    term = 'skin_group'
    ci = fit.conf_int()
    low, high = (float(v) for v in ci.loc[term])
    value = float(fit.params[term])
    p_value = float(fit.pvalues[term])

        "ci_high": float(np.exp(high)),

report.narrative: The original analysis estimated 1.17 (95% CI 1.05 to 1.3, p = 0.0046, n = 124,621) and returned the verdict BIAS DETECTED. The minimal flip changes Filter invalid dyads from "Keep dyads with both raters present and games>0" to "Keep dyads with at least 2 games together" and Bin skin tone into dark vs light from "Median split" to "Threshold at 0.5". The flipped universe estimates 1.12 (95% CI 0.98 to 1.29, p = 0.092, n = 61,822) and returns NO CLEAR EVIDENCE. An independent re-execution reproduced the flip. Robustness: 70% of the analysis grid agrees with the original verdict and 30% reverses it.
caveats: In 14 universes the model asked statsmodels for HC3 standard errors on a Logit fit; statsmodels computes HC0 (White) standard errors for such likelihood models whatever HC variant is asked, so those intervals and p-values are HC0, not the variant the option names.

Robustness headline: 70% of the analysis grid agrees with the original verdict (uniform random sample of the grid: 12 draws (each decision picks each of its options equally), 10 distinct results; independent of the beam search). Among the universes the search explored, 77% agree, but the beam search samples the universes that are closest to flipping, so that share leans toward flips.
